abstract: Interoperability between different vendors’ Internet Protocol (IP)-based solutions is absolutely vital to ensure smooth operation in professional audiovisual (AV) media facilities. Focusing on the control plane, this article describes some of the ways in which interoperability can be achieved including the use of open, freely available specifications, powerful and free-to-use automated testing tools, open-source software, and interoperability events. For vendors, all of these resources can play a valuable role during development to ensure the specifications are correctly implemented. For end users and systems integrators, using these testing tools before or as part of the selection of vendor solutions ensures unexpected issues are avoided during integration.

authors.bio: Robert Porter is a project manager with the Advanced Technology Team, Sony European Professional Engineering, Basingstoke, U.K. He received BEng and PhD degrees in electronic engineering from the University of Bristol, Bristol, U.K. He has been with Sony for 25 years, working in a range of areas including computer vision algorithms, video encoding, picture stitching, and edge computing. His current areas of interest are focused on supporting networked and cloud architectures for professional media.
